description.narrative: .To assist the Greater Amman Municipality (GAM) improve the quality of life for its citizens and comply with the National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP) via support for more sustainable resource-efficient urban planning .

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative:
1- Implementing a city database construction for Amman including energy, water and waste.
2- Establishing Sustainable Buildings Unit in the Jordan National Building Council.
3- Development of procedure manual for carrying out on-site inspections and retrofitting guidelines for contractors.
4- Updating Existing Building Energy Codes.
5- Development of an online tool for carrying out comparative socio-economic and environmental analysis of buildings using a life-cycle methodology.
6- Preparation of MRV system for Building Energy Codes.

1- A company has been awarded for implementing the retrofitting building thermal insulation and water efficiency measures.
2- A consulting company has been awarded for the implementation of a city database construction for Amman including energy, water and waste.
3- Sustainable Buildings Unit has been established in the Jordan National Building Council.
4- The procedure manual for carrying out on-site inspections and retrofitting guidelines for contractors have been developed and will be endorsed.
5- A partnership has been established for the development of an online tool for carrying out comparative socio-economic and environmental analysis of buildings using a life-cycle methodology.
6- The energy savings for lighting systems has been uploaded for MRV system established by Worldbank and will do the same for Building retrofitting projects once will be finalized.

1- Assist GAM in the collection, validation, and analysis of Energy, Water, and Waste data and establish a database for city indicators listed in the USF, SDG 11, and the WCCD to enhance GAM’s potential for planning and sustainable growth. 2- Develop External Lighting Code, Thermal Insulation Guideline for Existing Buildings, Green Buildings Code for Hospitals, Hydrology Code and updating the existing thermal Insulation Code. 3- Ensure the enforcement and compliance to the building codes through establishing a dedicated united at the Ministry of Public Works and Housing. The unit additionally should build the capacity of the unit staff and strengthen their capabilities in enforcing the building codes. 4- Eliminating, reducing or compensating the risks born by the private investor in Energy Efficiency in Buildings and consequently making investments in EE in buildings more attractive. 5- Reduce energy and water consumption in public buildings by utilizing the best practices for resource efficiency in the building sector, enable GHG emission reductions in three ways, namely through the reduction of electricity needed for space cooling; fossil fuel combustibles used for space heating; and water with a high embedded energy used in the building.

1. City Data Construction: Raw data for energy, water and waste has been collected from service providers, and 25 indicators for the city of Amman related to climate change were generated from the raw data, these indicators are according to Global platform for sustainable cities, Amman Urban observatory has been supported to adopt any indicators that are relevant to the reference indicators related to energy, water and material flows that will be attached to the Sustainability Plan. 2. An RPA has been signed with the Royal Scientific Society (RSS) regarding developing of “External Lighting Code”, “Thermal Insulation Guideline for Existing Buildings”, “Green Buildings Code for Hospitals”, “Hydrology Code” and updating the existing thermal Insulation Code. 3. Establishment of the Sustainable Buildings Unit (SBU) at the Jordan National Building Council (JNBC) in the Ministry of Public Works and Housing (MoPWH). The SBU is staffed with the necessary administrative and logistics support including test and inspection equipment. 4. Issuing the UNDP’s de-risking methodology (DEEI) report for Jordan and endorsed by Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (MEMR) for identification and quantification of the effectiveness of different policy and financial de-risking instruments for EE buildings. 5. Internal thermal insulation retrofitting of the third public building (the Ministry of Environment) has been completed including replacing the single glass old windows with double glazed thermal break windows according to the local thermal insulation building code in Jordan in addition to utilizing water efficiency fixtures.

1. Developing a database Integration Systems for Amman Urban Observatory at GAM to sustain the data collection automatically without the conventional methods of data collection, SURE will work with Amman Urban Observatory to develop database integration systems which will enable GAM’s users and administrators to update, retrieve, delete or arrange data within the established GIS-based database for city indicators to fulfill the data management and reporting needs. 2. Launching and endorsing an accreditation programme for Energy Service Companies (ESCOs) through the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources 3. Support the CDP-C40 task force by providing assistance in updating their GHG emissions inventory through a CC and GHG mitigation expert. Hence, a national consultant assigned support GAM’s task force in updating their GHG inventory, including creating a sustainable methodology including capacity building to enable GAM to update its inventory regularly and independently. 4. Testing DEEI for ESCO by 12 hotels in Aqaba. 5. Conducting state-of-the-art green residential building using EDGE. 6. Preparing NAMA proposal for JREEEEF as Super ESCO model in all governmental assets. 7. Direct emission reduction by retrofitting slaughterhouse at GAM for chiller replacement 280 tCO2e. 8. Capacity training for stakeholder using EDGE.
